body:
I believe names should be allowed even in cases where they are just simple numbers.

Especially problematic is that attempting to rename a point once triggers the name to change from a numeric-only string to something else, breaking compatibility with old project codes.

The concern here would be that users cannot know or control the index of the point array, so there is a possibility that the array index and the number might not match.

Therefore, as mentioned above, if we provide a way for users to control the array index, then as long as the names are unique, we should be able to accept even just numbers. Additionally, I believe we can avoid confusion by distinguishing the index display with colored (like yellow) text.

As mentioned above, I believe names with only simple number should be permitted. Furthermore, empty names should not be allowed, so this exception handling should be removed. Or just check `ERR_FAIL_COND_V(blend_points[p_point].name.is_empty(), String());`.

```suggestion
	String unique_name = _generate_unique_blend_point_name(blend_space, node->get_class().replace_first("AnimationNode", "");
```
To be clear and for consistency with StateMachineEditor.

I'm not sure I follow.

The intention here is for the name field be opt-in, and also locked in once created. The array index and the name being separate properties, with the name always taking precedence and never changing outside of user intervention is the new paradigm under this PR, and also what allows this to have backwards compatibility and not be a breaking change.

> Especially problematic is that attempting to rename a point once triggers the name to change from a numeric-only string to something else, breaking compatibility with old project codes.

Again, I'm not sure I follow. Clearing the name always reverts to index used as reference, and inline editing a point with only an index gives it a blank name, to start.

I think it would help me understand if you could tell me what you would prefer instead. If there is an index-based point that has its reference in code as `"parameters/BlendSpace1D/1/blend_position"`, what would you like a new point with the (string) name "1" to become, once I press enter? At the moment, it becomes "#1".

It can be "2", or "3", or whichever the next named index is.
Or it can be "1 2", like other names do.

It can't also be "1" though, because there's no way to distinguish between the two when referring to them via code.
Empty names are what allows the fallback to index to work. If empty names are no longer allowed, how will this PR not break older projects?

I means that when `AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D::set_blend_point_name(2, "1")` occurs, the name should be set to `1` instead of `#1` unless there is already a Node named `1` in the same Space.

If an empty name is used, simply reject the empty name instead of reverting to the index.

> It can't also be "1" though, because there's no way to distinguish between the two when referring to them via code.

I don't understand the meaning of this. What's seen in the code implies paths, but they are always valid only by name. Also, the function for getting points always looks only at the array index, while names are used to search for array indices, so their roles are distinct. There is no confusion between them, so there should be no restrictions on the names given to nodes.

Therefore, the number set in the name property is completely unrelated to the array index, so it doesn't need a `#` prefix. If an arbitrary name `777` is assigned to a point originally having path `parameters/BlendSpace1D/1/blend_position`, path `parameters/BlendSpace1D/1/blend_position` becomes invalid thereafter, and only `parameters/777/Jump/blend_position` remains valid.

Okay, but if index 1 has the name "1" and then the point with the index 0 (and no name yet) swaps indexes with "1", what would the new reference of the 0 node be, since the reference "1" is already taken?

> ...unless there is already a Node named `1` in the same Space.

What happens then?

It should either be a unique name or trigger an alert and be rejected. If based on NodeTreeDock behavior, the sequence number would increment to `2`. If based on AnimationPlayerEditor's animation addition, an alert would appear and the operation would be rejected.

This means older project script may be manipulating BlendSpace using path `parameters/blendspace2d/1/blend2/amount`. The problem arises when they change the name from `parameters/blendspace2d/1` to `parameters/blendspace2d/any` and then cannot revert it back to `parameters/blendspace2d/1` since now this PR make it `parameters/blendspace2d/#1`.

> If empty names are no longer allowed, how will this PR not break older projects?

BlendTree blending relies on subpaths, and without a name, the path cannot be created. This is why empty names are not permitted. There is no relationship between not allowing empty name and compatibility.

So in current BlendSpace2D, the index and name were _tentatively_ the same (in other words, it's just that numbers are used in the name), but since the index is not the name, it should not be returned by the get_name function as a fallback.

> The problem arises when they change the name from `parameters/blendspace2d/1` to `parameters/blendspace2d/any` and then cannot revert it back to `parameters/blendspace2d/1` since now this PR make it `parameters/blendspace2d/#1`.

I think you're misunderstanding something here. This isn't something this PR does, they can just clear the name to go back to the index reference, either through the toolbar, through inline edit, or through code. The empty name property is what allows the path reference to fallback into index.

If names can no longer be empty, _then_ the problem you describe arises. Not now. It also prevents anyone that relied on the index system in the past, with it self managing through `add_blend_point` and `remove_blend_point` to continue to use their blendspaces the same way.

I don't understand why you absolutely must fall back to the empty name in the index. The index and the name are completely separate things, residing in different domains. So it should be sufficient to simply disallow empty names and permit names simple number.

Current BlendSpace `add_blend_point()` and `remove_blend_point()` are also looking at an array index which is an `int` value, not retrieving a stringified number from the name.

If empty names are disallowed, does that mean once a point has a name, it must keep a name and use that name forever, and no longer be accessible via its index?
So projects edited after this PR, once they give a name to a blendspace point, can no longer clear or reset it to a prior state, with what used to be an automatically managed index for a reference that is subject to `add_blend_point` and `remove_blend_point`? How is this not a breaking change?

Are you implying cases where points are dynamically removed at runtime, causing the path to change? I don't think such cases occur frequently. However, if you're assuming that the path might change when the number of points changes and the same path indicates a different point entity depends on that changing path, the old index should match the array index. Therefore, the path name implemented by this PR should be retrievable with `get_blend_point_name()`.

Do we have any way of knowing that? The old system was clandestine but we can't discount that changing things in the way you recommend would be a breaking change for those cases, for someone that relied on indexes for whatever reason. If a point was inserted at in index in the middle of the array, all the following points would shift forward. Forcing names onto users will break something for someone, and lead to more unexpected behavior than now.

This PR in it's current state _does_ allow name and index to continue residing in different domains, and the lines of code highlighted here just elegantly allow for a fallback to index when the name isn't present, in cases where both are interchangeable.

For when the name is explicitly needed (null, not index when no name), `get_blend_point_stored_name` is what is called. Should I change the names of the functions instead, to make their roles clearer?

Also, while I would be happy to make a change here because no one disliked the prior index-only system as much as I did, I think backgrounding indexes as a concept is a bad idea, because of #66336. Users should be aware that indexes play a special role in BlendSpaces, even if that means keeping the (flawed) current paradigm intact. This PR simply heavily nudges users in the direction of having named blend points, and they really have to go out of their way to continue using indexes for reference.

Let's imagine there are points like the following:

```
A: parameters/blendspace2d/0
B: parameters/blendspace2d/1
C: parameters/blendspace2d/2
```

If A is deleted, the old system would look like this:

```
B: parameters/blendspace2d/0
C: parameters/blendspace2d/1
```

Indeed, if A is deleted on the new system might behave as follows when assigning a permanent name:

```
B: parameters/blendspace2d/1
C: parameters/blendspace2d/2
```

The migration path for this behavior change should be the `get_blend_point_name()` function.

```
B: parameters/blendspace2d/ + get_blend_point_name(0)　
C: parameters/blendspace2d/ + get_blend_point_name(1)　
```

These arguments should match the indices of the old system.

I assume there are no other locations in the core that permit empty name, and I believe there is no need for migration paths that duplicate roles.

These cases relying on this dynamic path should be quite niche. Furthermore, since a migration path is provided, I believe such minor compatibility breaks are acceptable (although we'll ultimately discuss it with the animation team).

Eventually, what you really need here is to add migration code to the setter so that when an old project is opened for the first time after this PR, and the name is empty, the index is used as the default name. Probably you can refer to the setter for AnimationPlayer. Then, remove the fallback, don't allow empty name and allow simple numeric names, I believe everything should be fine.
Okay, I understand. Let me know when there is a consensus and I'll make changes accordingly.
I've posted to [ContributorsChat](https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/animation) to open the discussion, so you can join if you're interested.

I will test it when I have time. By the way, if we modify the arguments of an existing bound method, we need to add a compatibility method to the compat file to pass CI.
